topic: GitHub Actions concurrency groups: default pending behavior vs cancel-in-progress, and when not to cancel
text:
Push three commits fast and GitHub Actions may silently skip the middle run. That's the default concurrency behavior, not a bug.

Per GitHub's docs, a concurrency group allows one running and at most one pending run. When a new run is queued, the existing pending one is canceled and replaced.

The group key decides what counts as "the same work":

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

My rule of thumb:

1. CI and tests: cancel-in-progress. Only the latest commit matters.
2. Deploys: don't cancel mid-flight. Let the running one finish, the newest waits.
3. Every run must execute: the docs list queue: max (up to 100 pending, FIFO), but it can't be combined with cancel-in-progress.

Canceling a half-finished deploy can leave an environment in a state nobody designed.

Which of your workflows would break if a run got canceled halfway?
